facts.title: The Battle of Sardarapat
facts.text: Forty kilometers west of Yerevan, on the Ararat plain, it halted the Ottoman invasion.

facts.title: Alexandropol falls
facts.text: After Kars. On what little land remained free: about 350,000 refugees who had fled the Armenian Genocide.

facts.title: Refusing to capitulate
facts.text: Aram Manukian overturned the decision to surrender the city without a fight and had its approaches fortified.

facts.title: The Catholicos stays
facts.text: George V Sureniants refused to flee and ordered the church bells to toll, summoning the people to resist.

facts.title: 9,000 to 10,000 men
facts.text: On the Armenian side, with 28 guns. Facing them: 7,500 to 10,000 soldiers and cavalrymen, with 40 artillery pieces.

facts.title: The counteroffensive
facts.text: Launched by Colonel Daniel Bek-Pirumian, it liberated Sardarapat and advanced 15 to 20 kilometers.

facts.title: The First Republic
facts.text: The stand at Sardarapat made its proclamation possible. A memorial has stood on the battlefield since 1968.

ytTitle: Sardarapat, May 1918: the battle that made the First Republic possible
ytLead: Fought from May 21 to 29, 1918, near Yerevan, the Battle of Sardarapat halted the Ottoman invasion and enabled the declaration of the First Republic of Armenia.
